senses.en: a belief, custom or way of doing things that has been passed from one generation to the next
examples: It is a **tradition** to visit relatives at Tet.
The family has kept this **tradition** for a hundred years.
By **tradition**, the youngest child speaks first.

forms.ex: **Traditional** food is served at the festival.

tradition.note: A **tradition** is older and passed down; a *custom* is simply what a group usually does. A *habit* belongs to one person.

senses.en: a person in your family who lived a long time before you
senses.vi: tổ tiên, ông bà tổ tiên
examples: We honour our **ancestors** on the death anniversary.
His **ancestors** came from a village in Ha Nam.
The altar holds photographs of our **ancestors**.

forms.ex: This is our **ancestral** home.

ancestor.note: Opposite: **descendant** (someone who comes after you). Stress the first syllable: **AN**-ces-tor.

senses.en: to show respect and love for a god or for your ancestors, especially through ceremonies
examples: Many Vietnamese families **worship** their ancestors.
People come here to **worship** at the temple.
The village **worships** a local guardian spirit.

senses.en: the act of showing respect and love for a god
examples: The pagoda is a place of **worship**.
Ancestor **worship** is common in Viet Nam.

senses.en: something such as food, flowers or money that is given as part of a religious ceremony
examples: The family placed fruit and flowers as **offerings** on the altar.
**Offerings** are made before the ceremony begins.
She brought an **offering** of rice and incense.

forms.ex: They **offer** fruit to their ancestors.

senses.en: a substance that produces a sweet smell when burned, used in religious ceremonies
examples: She lit three sticks of **incense**.
The temple smelled of **incense**.
Burning **incense** is part of the ritual.

incense.note: **Uncountable** — say *a stick of incense*, not *an incense*. Stress the first syllable: **IN**-cense.

senses.en: connected with the moon, or measured by the moon's cycle
senses.vi: thuộc về mặt trăng, âm lịch
examples: Tet is the **lunar** New Year.
The festival follows the **lunar** calendar.
The **lunar** month has about 29 days.

senses.en: a special day or period when people celebrate something, often with music, food and ceremonies
examples: The village holds a **festival** every spring.
The Mid-Autumn **Festival** is popular with children.
Thousands of people attend the **festival**.

senses.en: a set of actions always performed in the same way as part of a ceremony
examples: Lighting incense is an important **ritual**.
The **ritual** is performed before the meal.
Each family follows the same **ritual** at Tet.

senses.en: all the people in a family or society who are about the same age
examples: Three **generations** live in this house.
The recipe has been passed down for **generations**.
My grandmother's **generation** did things differently.

senses.en: a stage in the development of a product
examples: This is the fifth **generation** of the phone.
A new **generation** of electric cars is arriving.

senses.en: something that people avoid doing or talking about because it is thought to be wrong or offensive
examples: Sweeping the floor on the first day of Tet is a **taboo**.
In some cultures it is a **taboo** to point at people.
Money used to be a **taboo** subject at dinner.

senses.en: avoided because it is considered wrong or embarrassing
examples: Death is still a **taboo** topic in many families.
Those words are **taboo** in polite conversation.

taboo.note: Stress the second syllable: ta-**BOO**. Plural *taboos*.

senses.en: a belief that certain events or objects bring good or bad luck, not based on reason
senses.vi: sự mê tín, điều mê tín
examples: It is a common **superstition** that black cats bring bad luck.
Old **superstitions** are still strong in some villages.
He laughed and called it pure **superstition**.

forms.ex: My aunt is very **superstitious** about numbers.

senses.en: to cover something completely by folding paper, cloth or leaves around it
examples: We **wrap** the sticky rice cakes in banana leaves.
She **wrapped** the present in red paper.
**Wrap** the fish in foil before you cook it.

forms.en: the paper or material used to cover something
forms.ex: Take the **wrapping** off carefully.

wrap.note: The *w* is silent: /ræp/. Double the *p*: **wrapped**, **wrapping**. Sounds the same as *rap*.

senses.en: to make something look more attractive by adding things to it
examples: We **decorate** the house with peach blossom at Tet.
The children **decorated** the classroom for the festival.
The streets are **decorated** with red lanterns.

forms.en: something added to make a place look attractive
forms.ex: The **decorations** stay up for a week.

senses.en: to do something enjoyable to show that a day or an event is important
examples: We **celebrate** Tet with our whole family.
How do you **celebrate** your birthday?
The village **celebrated** the good harvest.

forms.vi: lễ kỷ niệm, sự ăn mừng
forms.ex: The **celebrations** lasted three days.

senses.en: to give knowledge, skills or objects to younger people so that they continue
examples: These songs have been **passed down** for generations.
My grandmother **passed** the recipe **down** to my mother.
The craft is **passed down** from parent to child.
colloc: passed down from generation to generation

pass down.note: Often in the passive: *the story **was passed down***. Compare *pass on* (give to the next person) and *pass away* (a polite way of saying *die*).

senses.en: to meet in order to spend time with each other
examples: The whole family **gets together** at Tet.
We **got together** at my aunt's house.
Let's **get together** after the exams.

forms.ex: We're having a small **get-together** on Sunday.

senses.en: the first person to enter a house in the new year, believed to bring good or bad luck for the year
senses.vi: người xông đất, người xông nhà
examples: The family chose a cheerful neighbour as their **first-footer**.
A good **first-footer** is said to bring luck all year.
Being the **first-footer** is a great responsibility.

first-footer.note: The custom itself is *first-footing*. In Viet Nam it is *xông đất* at Tet; the same belief exists in Scotland at New Year.

senses.en: to look at something and enjoy how beautiful or impressive it is
examples: We stopped on the bridge to **admire** the lanterns on the water.
Visitors come to the village to **admire** the blooming peach blossom.
She stood back and **admired** the decorated altar.

senses.en: to respect somebody for what they are or for what they have done
examples: I **admire** my grandmother for keeping every one of these customs alive.
The whole village **admires** the old drum maker.

forms.en: the feeling of admiring somebody or something
forms.ex: She spoke of her teacher with real **admiration**.

admire.note: Two different meanings that share one word: you **admire** a view with your eyes, and you **admire** a person with your respect. Stress the second syllable: ad-**MIRE**.

senses.en: to speak to a god, or to those you worship, to give thanks or to ask for something
examples: Many families go to the pagoda to **pray** for good luck at the start of the year.
My grandmother **prays** in front of the altar every morning.
They **prayed** for a good harvest and for the health of the elders.

forms.en: the words you say when you pray
forms.ex: He said a short **prayer** and lit the incense.

pray.note: **Pray for** what you want, not *pray something*. ✅ *pray for good luck* ❌ *pray good luck*. Do not confuse it with **prey** (an animal that is hunted) — the two sound the same.

senses.en: to make a person, an animal or a bad thing go away by frightening it
examples: The noise of the drums is meant to **chase away** bad spirits.
A bamboo pole in the yard **chases away** bad luck for the coming year.
The dogs **chased** the birds **away** from the rice.

chase away.note: Separable: *chase the birds away* and *chase away the birds* are both correct, but a pronoun must go in the middle — ✅ *chase them away*, ❌ *chase away them*.

senses.en: to let a person or an animal go free
examples: The referee **releases** a duck into the middle of the river.
Families **release** live carp into the lake before Tet.
The bird was **released** at the temple gate.

senses.en: to make a film, a record or a piece of news available to everyone
examples: The programme was **released** the week before the festival.
They **release** the results on Monday morning.

release.note: Stress the second syllable: re-**LEASE**, /rɪˈliːs/. The *s* at the end is /s/, not /z/.

senses.en: a being that people believe cannot be seen and brings harm or bad luck
examples: The lion dance is performed to drive **bad spirits** out of the house.
People once hung small bells on the pole to keep **bad spirits** away.
Nobody in the village will move house on that day, for fear of **bad spirits**.

bad spirit.note: Nearly always plural: *bad spirits*. In this sense **spirit** is a being, not the *spirit* that means someone's mood — compare *team spirit*.

senses.en: a long straight bamboo stem stood up in a yard at Tet and hung with small objects
examples: My uncle put up the **bamboo pole** on the morning of the twenty-third.
Small bells and lanterns hang from the **bamboo pole** in the yard.
The **bamboo pole** stays up until the seventh day of the new year.
colloc: hang something on a bamboo pole

bamboo pole.note: English has no single word for *cây nêu*, so this two-word phrase does the job; say what it is for when you use it with a foreign visitor.

senses.en: a small tree grown for how it looks rather than for fruit or wood
examples: He carried the **ornamental tree** home on the back of his motorbike.
A kumquat is the **ornamental tree** most families choose at Tet.
The **ornamental trees** are sold at the flower market for a week.

ornamental tree.note: **Ornamental** describes anything grown or made to be looked at: *an ornamental tree*, *an ornamental pond*. A tree grown for its fruit is a *fruit tree*.

senses.en: made or added to make something look attractive rather than to be useful
senses.vi: dùng để trang trí, có tính trang trí
examples: The pole is hung with **decorative** items: bells, small fish, and strips of red paper.
These bowls are **decorative** — nobody eats out of them.
She sewed a **decorative** border along the edge of the cloth.

forms.en: something added to make a place look attractive
forms.ex: The **decorations** go up a week before the festival.

decorative.note: **Decorative** is an adjective and goes before the noun: *decorative items*. Do not use it where you mean the verb — ❌ *we decorative the house* → ✅ *we **decorate** the house*.

senses.en: with flowers fully open
examples: People drive out to the flower village to photograph the **blooming** peach trees.
The **blooming** apricot branches were sold out by noon.
A **blooming** kumquat tree stood at the door of every house.

forms.ex: The apricot trees **bloom** in the first week of the lunar year.
The whole hillside was **in bloom**.

blooming.note: Use **blooming** before the noun (*blooming flowers*) and **in bloom** after the verb (*the flowers are in bloom*). ❌ *the flowers are blooming beautiful*.

senses.en: a large freshwater fish, kept in ponds and used in Vietnamese offerings
examples: The offerings include three live **carp** in a bowl of water.
On the twenty-third day, families release the **carp** into a river or a lake.
He caught a **carp** almost as long as his arm.

carp.note: The plural is usually **carp**, not *carps*: *three carp*. Like *fish*, *sheep* and *deer*.

senses.en: green rice picked before it hardens and then flattened, eaten as a delicacy in autumn
examples: The elders put a little **young rice** into each child's mouth and ask what they wish for.
**Young rice** is wrapped in lotus leaves and sold by the roadside in autumn.
Refusing **young rice** when an elder offers it would be rude.

young rice.note: Uncountable, like *rice* itself: *some young rice*, never *a young rice*. Vietnamese *cốm*; the Khmer name at the Ok Om Bok Festival is *om bok*.

senses.en: the formal part of a wedding, in which two people are married in front of their families
examples: A lion dance is often performed outside a **wedding ceremony**.
The **wedding ceremony** was held at the bride's family home.
Photographs of both **wedding ceremonies** hang in the front room.

wedding ceremony.note: The **wedding ceremony** is the formal part; the meal and the music afterwards are the *wedding reception* or simply *the wedding party*.

senses.en: an occasion when members of a family who live apart come together again
examples: The first day of Tet is a **family reunion** more than anything else.
Everyone travels home for the **family reunion**, however far it is.
We held a small **family reunion** at my aunt's house in July.

forms.en: to bring people together again after a time apart
forms.ex: Tet **reunites** families who have not met all year.

family reunion.note: Built from *re-* + *union*: a coming together **again**. The people already knew each other — a first meeting is not a reunion.

senses.en: the building of close feelings between members of a family by spending time together
senses.vi: sự gắn kết tình cảm gia đình
examples: These parties are a great time for **family bonding**.
Cooking the cakes together is really **family bonding**, not just work.
She says the long drive home is the best **family bonding** of the year.

forms.en: to form a close relationship with somebody
forms.ex: The two cousins **bonded** over a board game.
There is a strong **bond** between the three sisters.

family bonding.note: Uncountable — ❌ *a family bonding*. Related but not the same: *family bonds* (countable) are the connections themselves; *family bonding* is the making of them.

senses.en: somebody who goes to a festival
examples: The riverside was packed with **festival goers** by seven in the morning.
Drums, cheering, and a thousand **festival goers** all shouting at once.
Most of the **festival goers** had come from the next province.

festival goer.note: **-goer** builds freely: *a cinema goer*, *a churchgoer*, *a theatre goer*. Written as two words, or with a hyphen (*festival-goer*); both are accepted.

senses.en: somebody who takes part in a competition
examples: The **contestants** jump into the river to catch the duck.
Each **contestant** in the rice-cooking race has one hour.
Twelve **contestants** came from our village alone.

forms.ex: The rice-cooking **contest** starts at noon.

contestant.note: A **contestant** enters a contest; a *competitor* enters a competition or a race; a *candidate* sits an exam or stands for election.

senses.en: the traditional Asian fighting sports, such as karate, judo or Vietnamese vovinam
examples: The unicorn dancers are trained in **martial arts** as well as acrobatics.
He broke with family tradition by not practising **martial arts**.
**Martial arts** are taught in the yard behind the communal house.

martial arts.note: Plural in form and usually in agreement: *martial arts **are** popular*. The first word is /ˈmɑːʃl/ — no *r* sound in British English, and nothing to do with *marital*.

senses.en: difficult jumps, turns and balancing done as a performance
senses.vi: các động tác nhào lộn, xiếc
examples: Whoever wears the head has to be excellent at **acrobatics**.
The **acrobatics** at the end of the dance brought the crowd to its feet.
She learned **acrobatics** before she ever learned to dance.

forms.ex: Two **acrobats** balanced on a bamboo pole.
An **acrobatic** jump ended the performance.

acrobatics.note: Ends in *-s* but takes a singular verb: *acrobatics **is** hard on the knees*. Stress the third syllable: ac-ro-**BAT**-ics.

senses.en: a dance performed in a lion costume at New Year and other big occasions in several Asian countries
examples: A **lion dance** was performed at their opening ceremony.
The Japanese **lion dance** is called *shishi-mai*.
Two **lion dances** passed our street before breakfast.

lion dance.note: Say **do** or **perform** a lion dance, not *dance a lion dance*. The performers are a *lion dance troupe* or *team*.

senses.en: the Vietnamese dance performed in a *lân* costume at the Mid-Autumn and New Year Festivals
examples: The **unicorn dance** comes down our street on the night of the full moon.
A **unicorn dance** has a partner, *ông Địa*, who walks in front and fans the head.
The drum for the **unicorn dance** can be heard three streets away.

unicorn dance.note: *Múa lân* is translated into English in several ways — **unicorn dance** and *lion dance* are both used. Note the article: *a unicorn dance*, because *unicorn* begins with the consonant sound /j/.

senses.en: the custom among Vietnamese coastal fishing communities of honouring whales as protectors at sea
examples: **Whale worship** is practised in fishing villages all down the coast.
The tradition of **whale worship** goes back many generations here.
A temple for **whale worship** stands at the end of the beach.

whale worship.note: Uncountable. The verb pattern doubles the *p*: *the village has **worshipped** whales for centuries*.

senses.en: a man who lives in a temple or monastery and has given his life to his religion
examples: Keep quiet while the **monks** and the elders are talking.
A young **monk** swept the temple ground before the ceremony.
The **monks** eat their last meal of the day before noon.

monk.note: Rhymes with *drunk*; the *n* before /k/ is /ŋ/, so it is /mʌŋk/ — not /mʌnk/. The word for a woman is **nun**.

senses.en: long life, or the fact of living a long time
examples: Noodles are served at the party as a wish for **longevity**.
The old couple were given a red banner wishing them health and **longevity**.
Every one of these symbols stands for luck, wealth or **longevity**.

longevity.note: Uncountable and rather formal — in everyday speech people say *a long life*. Stress the second syllable: lon-**GEV**-ity, /lɒnˈdʒevəti/, with a /dʒ/ in the middle.

senses.en: on or near the sea shore, or belonging to it
senses.vi: thuộc miền ven biển, duyên hải
examples: Whale worship is a custom of the **coastal** provinces.
Our village is **coastal**, so the sea decides everything.
The festival is held in **coastal** towns from Da Nang southwards.

forms.ex: They drove the whole length of the **coast**.

coastal.note: The *oa* is one long sound, /əʊ/: **COAST**-al. Compare *inland* (away from the sea).

senses.en: the way you are expected to behave while eating with other people
examples: Tom asked Mai about Vietnamese **table manners** before the dinner.
Good **table manners** here start with waiting for the oldest person.
His **table manners** improved after a week at his grandmother's.

table manners.note: Always plural — ❌ *a table manner*. In this phrase **manners** means polite behaviour, not the *manner* that means a way of doing something.

senses.en: in the way something has been done for a long time; according to tradition
senses.vi: theo truyền thống, theo lệ xưa
examples: **Traditionally**, children in the US go from house to house asking for sweets at Halloween.
The pole is **traditionally** put up seven days before the new year.
This dish is **traditionally** eaten cold.

traditionally.note: Very often the first word of the sentence, with a comma after it: ***Traditionally**, we visit our father's family first.* That opening position is what makes it useful in writing.
